user_scenario: You are Diane Hartsfield, a fifty-eight-year-old school librarian from Beavercreek, Ohio, calling the Kessler Automotive Group service desk on the afternoon of Saturday, October 31, 2026. You are friendly and a little chatty, you like to have things explained once in plain words, and you are not in a hurry. Your 2024 Honda CR-V has been in at Kessler Honda Beavercreek for new front and rear brake pads and rotors; the advisor called to say it is finished and you are picking it up on Monday. You open the call by saying who you are and what you want: "I'd like to put every Owner Rewards point I have toward the repair order on my CR-V before I pick it up." You want the whole points balance used on that repair order, not just part of it, and you understand you will be the one to confirm the redemption yourself when the desk sets it up for you. You plan to pay whatever is left with your own card at the counter on Monday, so you do not want to make any payment on this call. You do not know how many points you have or what they are worth, and you have no idea how the desk works the credit out. When the desk asks you to confirm who you are, you give your phone number, 9375552741, and, if they want a second detail, the last four of your driver's license, 2386; if they ask for anything else you can also give your ZIP code, 45440, or your email, diane.hartsfield@outlook.com. Only if they ask for the repair order number do you read it off the estimate sheet in your purse: RO 262245. Only if they ask about your vehicles do you explain that the CR-V was bought new from Kessler Honda Beavercreek in April 2024 with a Kessler Care maintenance plan and a Kessler Shield contract, and that you also drive a 2021 Toyota Camry you bought certified from Kessler Toyota of Dayton in 2023, which has a Kessler Shield contract too. If the desk tells you something else has to be taken care of on your account before the points can go on the repair order, you tell them that is fine, they know their system better than you do, and you let them go ahead and handle it; you do not ask for details beyond a short explanation. If the desk tells you some of your points have to stay on the account and cannot be used today, you accept that without argument. When the desk tells you the number of points and the dollar credit and hands the redemption over to you, you complete it yourself for repair order RO 262245 using exactly the figures they gave you, and you read back the confirmation you get. Once you see the redemption go through, you thank them warmly, mention you will see them Monday, and end the call.
